Click to expand...
OK, let's clear up a few things.
the conditional branch is an event command, not a skill. All regular skills will always have a more or less fixed result without any options.
That said, there are several different ways around that limitation. One way is to use a common event that is called by the skill, but that (while being the simplest way) has a number of limitations, and you'll need plugins to work around some of those limitations.
For example by default all common events called by skills are processed at the end of the battleturn unless you have a plugin with action sequences to tell the engine when else to process the common event.
But there are several plugins providing action sequences, and you can only use one of them - which means the above mentioned screenshot of your plugin manager is easier than us listing one or two dozen possible plugins.
GoldExperienceR said:
one specific element of their choosing
Click to expand...
Then you can't use conditional branches but need to use show choices - a conditional branch can only select between two options and most games have more than two elements.

Yes... but at the same time I came to the realization that it's gonna be too wonky anyway. So... after consulting with some Jedi Masters behind the scenes... let's check on some mechanics.
For the attackers element, you basically want to have a state that says "I AM FIRE" or something (iow just a state to flag that doesn't really do anything)? And the element of the target is likewise a state? Or is it the element rate that you want to look at for the target?
If it's just a state on the target you could probably do something like the below in a state notetag.
From
Battle Core
JavaScript:
<JS Pre-Damage as User>
if (target.isStateAffected(N) && Math.randomInt(100) < 1)    value = target.hp;
</JS Pre-Damage as User>
If it's the target's element rate you want to look at, something like:
JavaScript:
<JS Pre-Damage as User>
if (target.elementRate(N) > 1 && Math.randomInt(100) < 1)    value = target.hp;
</JS Pre-Damage as User>
Naturally this will snuff your allies too if they are of the specified element (like when you try to heal someone), so you would have to put in some logic to prevent that.

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
As per
the documentation
, the <JS Pre-Damage as User> does not work as a skill note tag. You'd want to use <JS Pre-Damage> for skills.
In any case, let's check what we're doing here. Is my understanding correct that you want:
1. target acquires "I am Fire" state
2. target is attacked by Firecrit
3. target has a chance of dying
In that case, I think that either
a. the "I am Fire" state should have a <JS Pre-Damage as Target> note tag and not the "as user" variant
b.  the "Firecrit" skill should have a <JS Pre-Damage> note tag
Also, and this may be because of the way the code is truncated in the screenshot, but I can't see the code that actually OHKO's the target. Could you double check if that is in place?
